function: Joint learned design of BS precoding matrix and IRS phase shifts (active and passive beamforming) maximizing the minimum achievable secrecy rate under imperfect CSI (pp. 5-6).
system: Downlink: 6-antenna BS, passive 8-element IRS (unit modulus), two 2-antenna devices, one 2-antenna Eve; Rician links, imperfect CSI; frequency band not stated (pp. 4, 11).
method: Reinforcement learning: actor-critic with a conditional diffusion model generating the precoder and IRS phases (AC-GDM), trained from environment reward; DDPG and TD3 as baselines (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: large-scale Rician fading, ULA steering vectors, Gaussian CSI error; training samples randomly generated from the model, testing on newly generated ones; no dataset (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Training and test samples i.i.d. from one Rician model; sweeps over Rice factor, Eve distance, IRS elements, antennas, power, devices, CSI error; no cross-setting test stated (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Learned: DDPG [33] and TD3 [37]; non-learned: conventional BF and AN schemes without IRS, optimization method not described (pp. 10, 12).
metrics: Mean and standard deviation of minimum achievable secrecy rate (MASR) and maximum eavesdropping rate (MER); convergence reward and training steps (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Time complexity O(lNXH^2SA) for AC-GDM versus O(lXH^2SA) for DDPG; l iterations, N denoising steps, X samples per iteration (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 10: "all channels are modeled using large-scale Rician fading". Own simulator with a textbook Rician model and ULA steering vectors; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channels.
q2_support: p. 10: "training and testing data samples are independently and identically distributed". Test data come from the same model; pretraining and fine-tuning is only suggested for real deployment (p. 12), and no model is tested in an unseen setting.
q3_support: p. 10: "we employ the DDPG and twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithms as baseline algorithms". Non-learned: p. 12 "compared to conventional BF and AN schemes" (Figs. 9-10); DDPG and TD3 are compared in Figs. 11-17, all on MASR.
q4_support: p. 9: "The time complexity of the AC-GDM algorithm is analyzed as follows". It gives O(lNXH^2SA) for AC-GDM against O(lXH^2SA) for DDPG.
q5_support: p. 10: "randomly generated based on the channel fading model". Own simulation; no code or data link, no public dataset or measurements, hardware tests only planned (p. 15).
notes: Area 3: the learned agent outputs the BS precoder and IRS phase shifts (action = {T, v}, p. 6); secrecy is the objective, not a separate function. q3 is the closest call: BF and AN benchmarks are called conventional and have no IRS, but how their precoders are optimized is never stated (p. 12), so the reviewer should confirm they are non-learned. No numerical-optimization baseline is run (p. 10).
